answer_sql:
WITH per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  GROUP BY
    customer_key
), labelled AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    CASE
      WHEN first_order_date < CAST('2023-12-31' AS DATE)
      THEN '(a) existing — purchased before 31.12.2023'
      WHEN first_order_date > CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      THEN '(b) new — first purchased after 01.01.2024'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM per_customer
)
SELECT
  g.customer_group,
  ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
JOIN labelled AS g
  USING (customer_key)
WHERE
  NOT g.customer_group IS NULL
GROUP BY
  g.customer_group
ORDER BY
  revenue DESC

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: Two rows: how much money Contoso has ever taken, after discount, from each of two groups of people. The 41,390 customers who were already buying before 31 December 2023 have paid 193,042,649.52 USD. The 10,782 whose very first purchase came after 1 January 2024 have paid 25,732,927.48 USD. Each figure is that group's WHOLE buying history rather than only the period that defined the group, so (a)'s total includes the 35,167,849.45 those existing customers went on to spend in 2024 and 2025. The period covered is 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, the full extent of order dates in this bundle, and both the web shop and the physical shops are counted. WHAT IS NOT IN THESE FIGURES: discount, which is already deducted — gross would be 205,222,088.74 and 27,337,846.80; the 17 buyers whose first purchase fell on or between the two cut-off days, worth 38,894.66, who are in neither row; and the 52,801 people on the customer register who have never bought anything, who have no revenue to report. THE COMPARISON IS NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE ON TIME: group (a) has had up to ten years to spend and group (b) about two, which is why per customer — 4,663.99 against 2,386.66 — the gap narrows from 7.5-to-1 to 2.0-to-1.

WITH per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date

      THEN 'a'
      WHEN first_order_date > CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      THEN 'b'
    END AS grp
  FROM per_customer
)
SELECT
  ROUND(
    SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
      g.grp = 'a') - SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
      g.grp = 'b'),
    2

JOIN labelled AS g
  USING (customer_key)

  NOT g.grp IS NULL

MUCH OF THIS GAP IS TIME, NOT LOYALTY: group (a) has had up to ten years to accumulate and group (b) about two, and per customer the gap is only 2,277.34 (4,663.99 against 2,386.66), a ratio of 2.0 rather than 7.5. NOT INCLUDED: the 17 buyers between the cut-offs, the 52,801 registered customers who never bought, and discount, which is already deducted from both sides.

turns.why: Compute the revenue gap between the two cohorts, and price the same gap under the windowed reading, so the difference is reported with the one fork that can move it.
turns.did:
WITH per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  GROUP BY
    customer_key
), labelled AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    CASE
      WHEN first_order_date < CAST('2023-12-31' AS DATE)
      THEN 'a'
      WHEN first_order_date > CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      THEN 'b'
    END AS grp
  FROM per_customer
), totals AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
      g.grp = 'a') AS a_lifetime,
    SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
      g.grp = 'b') AS b_lifetime,
    SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
      g.grp = 'a' AND l.order_date < CAST('2023-12-31' AS DATE)) AS a_windowed,
    COUNT(DISTINCT l.customer_key) FILTER(WHERE
      g.grp = 'a') AS a_customers,
    COUNT(DISTINCT l.customer_key) FILTER(WHERE
      g.grp = 'b') AS b_customers
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN labelled AS g
    USING (customer_key)
  WHERE
    NOT g.grp IS NULL
)
SELECT
  ROUND(a_lifetime - b_lifetime, 2) AS difference_lifetime,
  ROUND(a_lifetime / b_lifetime, 2) AS times_larger_lifetime,
  ROUND(a_windowed - b_lifetime, 2) AS difference_if_windowed,
  ROUND(a_windowed / b_lifetime, 2) AS times_larger_if_windowed,
  ROUND(a_lifetime / a_customers - b_lifetime / b_customers, 2) AS difference_per_customer
FROM totals
